exec
"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command '$a=Get-Content docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-mirror-identity-window-design.md; for($i=0;$i -lt $a.Count;$i++){ '"'{0}:{1}' -f ("'$i+1),$a[$i] }' in C:\Temp\pxr4
 succeeded in 179ms:
1:# Design: the review mirror's identity window
2:
3:**Filed 2026-09-05.** Reported from a session running the plugin against
4:KitnEssentials, which hit repeated `BLOCKED: the source status changed
5:since construction` refusals and could not tell why.
6:
7:## The measured facts
8:
9:1. `Get-StatusSha256` (`tools/new-review-mirror.ps1:662`) fingerprints a
10:   repo as the fields of `git status --porcelain --ignored -uall -z`
11:   PLUS the content manifest of the paths that listing names. Not every
12:   path: `Get-ManifestSubject` omits a deletion-only entry, which has no
13:   bytes to hash.
14:   `Get-ContentManifest` (`:576`) expands a directory subject
15:   recursively, so a single `!! .claude/` status entry pulls the bytes of
16:   every file beneath it into the digest.
17:2. The content half is deliberate and the function says so: editing an
18:   already-ignored file leaves the status listing byte-identical, so a
19:   list-only digest would pass through exactly the tampering the check
20:   exists to catch.
21:3. The build-time `source_status_sha256` is re-checked at THREE points
22:   against the same recorded value:
23:   - `-Prepare` step 1a, `tools/dispatch-round.ps1:457`
24:   - the wrapper, before the client runs, `tools/dispatch-round.ps1:275`
25:   - the wrapper, after the client finishes,
26:     `tools/dispatch-round.ps1:310`, `throw 'the mirror changed while the
27:     round ran'`
28:4. Therefore the exposed window is **mirror build to wrapper exit**, not
29:   build to prepare. It spans the whole round.
30:5. The refusal names no path. `tools/new-review-mirror.ps1:846` prints the
31:   class of change and stops.
32:6. Nothing in `skills/` states the constraint. This repo's `CLAUDE.md`
33:   carries a quiet-period rule covering `-Prepare` to wrapper exit only,
34:   and says in its own text that no prose rule in `skills/` carries it.
35:   The plugin therefore does not take the rule to the repos it is
36:   installed into.
37:
38:## What the reporting session proposed, and why it is not the fix
39:
40:The report proposed fusing the mirror build and `-Prepare` into one
41:command. That fusion is CONSTRUCTIBLE: one script could build, read the
42:probe's reported override hash, generate the wrapper body from it, and
43:then prepare. An earlier draft of this document called it impossible,
44:which was wrong, and cross-vendor review of that draft said so.
45:
46:It is refused on a different ground. It closes the first of three windows
47:and leaves the largest one open. A round that takes ten minutes still
48:voids if an ignored file moves while the reviewer reads. Buying the small
49:window at the cost of a more complex build, while the round-length window
50:stays exactly as it was, is not the trade this defect calls for.
51:
52:The ordering the fusion would have to respect is real and worth writing
53:down, because it constrains any future attempt: the build runs the client
54:context probe, the probe writes the verified override file, and the
55:wrapper body embeds that file's SHA256
56:(`skills/multi-model-verify/SKILL.md`, the `verified-override-dispatch`
57:region). So the build must complete before the wrapper body can exist,
58:and the body must exist before `-Prepare` can install it.
59:
60:The real constraint is a QUIET PERIOD over the reviewed repository, from
61:the build until the wrapper exits.
62:
63:## Decisions
64:
65:**D1. The gate does not change.** No path is removed from the digest, no
66:carve-out is added, and no re-mint or reseal mode is introduced. A
67:volatile-path allowlist was considered and rejected for this cycle: the
68:directories that move on their own (`.claude/`, `.codex/`) are instruction
69:surfaces, and excluding an instruction surface from the tamper net defeats
70:the check. It is recorded as an open backlog item, not built.
71:
72:**D2. The refusal explains itself, advisorily.** The build writes the
73:SOURCE side's content manifest to a SIBLING of the mirror directory,
74:`<MirrorPath>.source-manifest`. On the source-status refusal path only,
75:`-VerifyIdentity` reads that file and names the paths whose content
76:changed and the paths that entered or left manifest coverage.
77:
78:The advisory file is safe by construction and must stay that way:
79:
80:- It is read ONLY after the comparison has already decided to block, so
81:  it can never turn a refusal into a pass. A missing, unreadable,
82:  truncated, or deliberately corrupted file changes the printed
83:  explanation and never the exit code.
84:- It is a sibling, not a child, of the mirror and lives outside the
85:  repository, so it enters neither `source_status_sha256` nor
86:  `mirror_state_sha256`.
87:- It pins nothing, which is why it may be a file at all. The header's
88:  rule that identity values are passed as arguments rather than re-read
89:  from a file the build wrote applies to values that PIN something; this
90:  one carries no authority.
91:
92:**D2a. Its DESTINATION joins BOTH of the guard blocks `-OverrideOut`
93:already sits in, and nothing is removed until they all pass.** Cross-vendor review of the first draft found that writing to a
94:derived path with no guard is itself a write into an unknown file: a hard
95:link or symbolic link at that path would carry the write through to its
96:target, and a target inside the repository would be corrupted by the very
97:function that exists to explain a corrupted repository. The same review
98:found that an explicitly supplied `-OverrideOut <MirrorPath>.source-
99:manifest` passes today's checks and would then be overwritten, breaking
100:the wrapper's override hash.
101:
102:The default override path is already a sibling of exactly this shape,
103:`<MirrorPath>.skills-override.txt`. Its protection sits in TWO places,
104:and round 1 of this plan's debate found that a draft claiming to copy
105:"the override's whole guard set" had copied only the first:
106:
107:- the LEXICAL block (`tools/new-review-mirror.ps1:951-1008`): overlap
108:  with the repository and the mirror, pre-existence, path budget;
109:- the ALIAS block (`:1258-1290`): walk the path's ancestors for a
110:  reparse point, and check it against every followed link target.
111:
112:The sidecar joins both, plus an overlap check against the override path
113:and against every declared `-ExtraInput`.
114:
115:**The extra-input check refuses what it cannot decide.** Spelling
116:equality is not filesystem identity. With `C:\alias` a junction to
117:`C:\out`, a mirror at `C:\out\mirror` and an extra input at
118:`C:\alias\mirror.source-manifest`, both output paths have ordinary
119:ancestors and pass their own alias checks, while the extra input keeps
120:the alias spelling and compares unequal. `-Force` would then remove the
121:file that extra input names. This tool cannot establish physical identity
122:there, so an extra input reached through a directory link is REFUSED
123:rather than compared.
124:
125:**Validation completes before anything is removed.** The same round found
126:that a draft deleting a pre-existing sidecar under `-Force` inside the
127:lexical block would delete it BEFORE the alias block refuses an aliased
128:mirror path, so a build that was going to be rejected had already
129:destroyed a file. The removal moves after every check.
130:
131:**A root and a resolution failure are different answers.** The helper
132:returns one of three kinds, `ok`, `root` or `error`. A draft returned the
133:same null for both, so both callers announced "filesystem root".
134:Measured 2026-09-05: Windows PowerShell 5.1's provider accepted a
135:278-character absolute path that `GetFullPath` refused with
136:`PathTooLongException`, while PowerShell 7 accepted it, so on 5.1 a
137:long-path build would have reported a filesystem root and never reached
138:the path-budget refusal that names the real problem.
139:
140:**A root is detected through the framework, not through the leaf.**
141:Measured 2026-09-05: `Split-Path 'C:\' -Leaf` returns `C:\`, not `C:`, so
142:a regex on the leaf never fires for a drive root; and
143:`Split-Path '\\server\share\' -Leaf` returns `share` with parent
144:`\\server`, which rejoined would name a DIFFERENT SHARE. The two hosts
145:disagree on the UNC case. So `GetPathRoot` decides, and the suffix is
146:appended to the full path rather than rejoined to a parent.
147:
148:**Create-new bounds the final component only.** It stops an overwrite and
149:a link substituted at that name. It cannot defend a DIRECTORY component:
150:an ancestor replaced by a junction before the open redirects creation
151:into that junction's target, and no open flag prevents it. The alias
152:block is what covers ancestors. The design states that division rather
153:than letting create-new appear to cover both.
154:
155:**D2b. The explanation states only what the comparison measures, and the
156:reader enforces every bound it advertises.** Two rounds of review found
157:overstatements here, each one an instance of the very class this cycle
158:exists to remove. The corrected behaviour is part of this design rather
159:than a detail of it:
160:
161:- Manifest membership is not file existence. A deletion-only entry is
162:  omitted from the manifest by `Get-ManifestSubject`
163:  (`tools/new-review-mirror.ps1:460-463`), and a clean tracked file that
164:  becomes dirty ENTERS it. So the groups are named `entered manifest
165:  coverage` and `left manifest coverage`, never `appeared` and
166:  `vanished`.
167:- No content difference does not prove the status listing changed. A
168:  replaced sidecar produces the same empty result. The fallback says the
169:  advisory manifest did not identify the cause, and stops there.
170:- A malformed record is reported, never silently dropped. That requires
171:  CHECKING THE GRAMMAR: a draft that only rejected a missing separator
172:  accepted `bad.txt not-a-hash` as an ordinary record, so a truncated
173:  digest became a reported difference instead of an admission of
174:  incompleteness. The hash field is validated, and duplicates and
175:  over-long records are counted.
176:- An EMPTY line is a malformed record, with no special case. A draft
177:  skipped every empty string as "the trailing split artifact", which
178:  silently dropped leading and interior empty records too. Records are
179:  read with a `StringReader`, which returns nothing at all for a file
180:  ending in a newline, so the artifact does not exist to special-case.
181:  The fix removes the condition rather than refining it.
182:- TRUNCATION IS ITS OWN STATE, never a malformed count. A draft capped
183:  the record loop by incrementing the malformed counter once and
184:  abandoning the remainder, so 200,003 malformed records reported
185:  200,001 and a resource limit was reported as a grammar diagnosis. The
186:  reader reports truncation, and says the remainder was not examined.
187:- The cap applies DURING extraction. A `-split` materializes every line
188:  of a file whose size is someone else's choice before any later cap can
189:  matter, so the bound has to live in the reader that produces the
190:  records.
191:- The size limit bounds THE READ. A draft measured the file with
192:  `Get-Item` and then read it with a separate `ReadAllBytes`, which
193:  bounds nothing, and `Get-Item`'s failure is non-terminating in a script
194:  that never sets `$ErrorActionPreference`, so an unreadable file left
195:  the test unmade and carried on. One handle now measures and reads. The
196:  record count and record length are bounded too, because a byte limit
197:  alone does not bound the working set a split produces.
198:- Untrusted text is rendered by UNICODE CATEGORY, not by a numeric
199:  range. `[int]$ch -lt 32` passes the C1 controls U+0085 and U+009B,
200:  which are terminal escape introducers, and passes U+2028 and the
201:  bidirectional override U+202E. Control, Format, LineSeparator,
202:  ParagraphSeparator and Surrogate cover them by name, and the sidecar
203:  path and any exception message go through the same renderer.
204:- The reader does not resolve links, and the design says so rather than
205:  implying otherwise. Worst case it prints misleading names from an
206:  unrelated file, which is why every emitted comparison is introduced as
207:  unauthenticated and advisory, and why the refusal never depends on it.
208:
209:**D3. The quiet period ships in the skill.** A contract region states it,
210:covering build through wrapper exit, so it travels with the plugin.
211:
212:The region states the operational rule AND its measurement limits,
213:because a contract region that claims more than its mechanism delivers is
214:the defect class this whole cycle is about. Three limits, all found by
215:cross-vendor review of the first draft:
216:
217:- The check samples endpoints. A change made and reverted inside the
218:  round is not detected, and no before-and-after check could detect it
219:  (`tools/dispatch-round.ps1:305-307` says so already).
220:- A tracked file that git reports CLEAN is covered by neither
221:  fingerprint, so a raw-byte change surviving the clean filter is not

53:## Long-running commands
54:
55:DISPATCH DEBATE ROUNDS AND FULL GATES IN THE BACKGROUND, from the FIRST
56:attempt. The reason is VISIBILITY, not survival, and the difference
57:matters because the reason written here before was false. A foreground
58:call OWNS the session: while it runs, nobody can see the round, talk to
59:the agent, or redirect it. A backgrounded call leaves the session
60:answering, which is the property measured in
61:`docs/superpowers/plans/rounds/2026-08-31-completion-coupled-dispatch/benefit-measurement.md`.
62:
63:THE 600-SECOND CEILING DOES NOT KILL. Measured 2026-09-01 on Claude Code
64:2.1.251: a foreground call that ran past it was MOVED to the background
65:by the harness under a new task id and completed with exit 0. The
66:measured case was a local filesystem command rather than a codex round,
67:so what it establishes is narrow and stated narrowly - the ceiling is not
68:a kill. The text here previously said a crossing round is killed with the
69:quota spent for nothing, and cited "measured repeatedly through 0.21.x";
70:that claim is withdrawn, and this rule no longer rests on it.
71:
72:Two traps in the dispatch scripts themselves, both measured 2026-08-04:
73:
74:- Do NOT run the native `codex` call under
75:  `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. codex prints a benign models-cache
76:  warning to stderr at startup, and Stop promotes ANY native stderr line
77:  to a terminating `NativeCommandError`, killing the dispatch before the
78:  reviewer does any work. Drop to `Continue` around the native call and
79:  check `$LASTEXITCODE` yourself; nothing is being ignored, only the
80:  stderr channel is stopped from masquerading as a failure.
81:- Do NOT pipe an expensive run's output through `tail`, `head` or
82:  `Select-Object -Last`. The failure NAMES are what a second run needs,
83:  and truncating them costs the whole run again.
84:- The brief must be read as STRICT UTF-8 and `$OutputEncoding` set to
85:  UTF-8 at SCRIPT scope before the pipe, restored in `finally`. Measured
86:  2026-08-11: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a no-BOM file with the ANSI
87:  code page AND defaults `$OutputEncoding` to us-ascii, so one em dash
88:  reaches the reviewer as THREE question marks and it answers a brief you
89:  never sent. `Get-Content -Raw | codex exec` is the defective form. A
90:  `& { }` block does NOT work: the native pipe reads the OUTER scope, so
91:  a child-scope assignment is scoped and inert. Only the round-evidence
92:  binding catches the corruption, and it costs the whole round.
93:  0.23.0 fixed the SKILL.md dispatch ONLY. `tools/check-drift.ps1:1060`
94:  still ships the defective form, with no brief binding to catch it, and
95:  `commands/doctor.md:70` has the same shape on a pure-ASCII payload.
96:  Both are named in the finding write-up under
97:  `docs/superpowers/plans/rounds/2026-08-11-budget-flake-generator/`;
98:  do not read the rule above as a statement that the repo is clean.
99:
100:**The dispatch is no longer a copied snippet, and the tool no longer
101:starts anything.** `tools/dispatch-round.ps1` has two modes, and every
102:lane calls it rather than writing its own.
103:
104:`-Prepare` builds the round as one fail-closed transaction: verify the
105:working directory IS the named review mirror, resolve the host, hash the
106:prior state, reserve the dispatch directory, install the lane's body and
107:the wrapper around it, and write the receipt last of all. It then PRINTS
108:the exact command line and the task name, and starts NO process. The
109:caller dispatches that command as a harness background command.
110:
111:`-Classify` is the wrapper's own final act, and this is the sentence that
112:carries the design: THE WRAPPER'S EXIT CODE IS THE CLASSIFICATION. `0`
113:means `reply-present` and nothing else; `2` is a parameter-binding or
114:internal failure; `1` is every other state, named on the wrapper's last
115:stdout line. A wrapper that does not reach its final statement cannot
116:report success, whatever its directory holds. Measured 2026-09-01: a
117:round killed after publishing a zero exit file AND a non-empty reply
118:reported `[killed]`, and left a reservation no later caller could redeem.
119:Never re-read the dispatch directory to decide a verdict.
120:
121:Written here as a plain repo-relative path: `CLAUDE.md` is neither skill
122:body, where the harness substitutes `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, nor a lane's
123:command literal, where `references/backup-lane.md` carries a
124:session-filled `<plugin-checkout>` placeholder instead. The full contract
125:lives in five regions in
126:`skills/multi-model-verify/references/model-prompting-notes.md`:
127:`round-dispatch-tool`, `round-dispatch-states`,
128:`round-dispatch-exit-map`, `round-dispatch-operation`, and
129:`background-task-naming`.
130:
131:Name every backgrounded call for the person watching it. A reviewer round
132:leads with its LANE and ROUND, as in `Astra R1 debate round` or
133:`Kimi R2 debate round`. A gate or a mirror build has no lane, so it leads
134:with its KIND instead, as in `Gate: pytest 5.1` or `Mirror build`.
135:`-Prepare` now PRINTS the name, so the convention has a source; nothing
136:enforces its use.
137:
138:**DO NOT TOUCH THE REVIEWED TREE BETWEEN `-Prepare` AND THE WRAPPER'S
139:EXIT.** The wrapper verifies the mirror's identity after the round runs,
140:and the source fingerprint is built from what `git status` names, so a new
141:UNTRACKED file is enough to fail it. The round then classifies as `1`, its
142:reply is not evidence, and the quota is spent for nothing. Measured
143:2026-09-04: writing six documentation files into the repo mid-round voided
144:a completed cross-vendor round, and the remedy cost a second dispatch, so
145:the price was two rounds. The gate is in `tools/dispatch-round.ps1`; NO
146:prose rule in `skills/` carries it, which is why it is written here. Queue
147:edits until the wrapper exits, however small and however unrelated they
148:look.
149:
150:**WRITE EVERY BRIEF TO DISK BEFORE SENDING IT**, both lanes, outside the
151:reviewed tree. The codex lane gets this free, because the dispatch pipes a
152:file. The same-harness lane does NOT: a brief sent as an agent message
153:leaves no artifact, and it cannot be retained afterwards. Measured in the
154:same debate: seven of that lane's briefs are permanently unrecoverable, so
155:the record can show what one lane was asked and not the other. A scratchpad

158:## Dev loop
159:The plugin is installed user-scope from a LOCAL marketplace pointing at
160:this working copy, but installs are VERSIONED CACHE COPIES — checkout
161:edits are NOT live until you: bump `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, run
162:`claude plugin marketplace update parallax`, THEN
163:`claude plugin update parallax@parallax` (qualified name required),
164:and restart the session when hooks/ or skills/ changed. A restart alone
165:only reloads the cached version. The marketplace refresh is load-bearing:
166:the directory-source catalog is read at session start, so with it skipped
167:the update sees the OLD version and silently does nothing — measured
168:2026-08-17, the same command copied nothing before the refresh and
169:installed 0.26.1 after it. GitHub remote (Bmwascher/parallax, public)
170:serves stable installs on other machines.
171:
172:BUMP THE VERSION AFTER THE DIFF DEBATE, not when the branch's first task
173:touches it and not merely as the last BUILD task. `plugin update` keys
174:ONLY on the version string: once a version has been cached, the same
175:number reports "already at the latest version" and copies NOTHING,
176:however much the checkout changed afterwards. Measured 2026-08-03: 0.20.0
177:was bumped mid-branch, cached at 14:13, and then five diff-debate rounds
178:rewrote `skills/`. Measured again 2026-08-16: 0.26.0 bumped LAST in the
179:build, exactly as this rule then read, and six debate rounds still moved
180:the tree after the bump was cached — the installed copy was five commits
181:stale and missing fixes the release existed to ship. The debate is what
182:moves the tree after the final build task, so "last" means after it; a
183:bump consumed before the branch is finished recovers only by another bump
184:(that is what 0.26.1 is).
185:
186:VERIFY THE INSTALL BY CONTENT, never by the cache directory's name: a
187:directory named `0.26.0` held code from five commits before the shipped
188:head. The cheap check is `gitCommitSha` in
189:`~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, which records exactly which
190:commit was copied; the thorough one is hashing the cached files against
191:the checkout with CRLF normalized. Backlog item 65 holds the full record
192:and the open question of a mechanical check.

194:## Skill editing rules
195:The multi-model-verify skill's transport commands (codex exec flags, resume
196:syntax) are LIVE-VERIFIED contracts locked by evals/multi-model-verify/
197:test_multi_model_verify.py — change the tests first (they encode review
198:findings), then the skill.
199:
200:The reviewer's isolation flags (`--disable plugins --disable apps`) and the
201:context probe's failure directions are live-verified contracts locked by
202:`evals/multi-model-verify/test_multi_model_verify.py` and
203:`test_codex_context_probe.py`. Change the tests first. Every failure
204:direction in the probe lands on BLOCKED; a change that lets an unmade
205:measurement read as clean is the one outcome these scripts may never
206:produce.
207:
208:The backup lane's credential handling is a live-verified contract locked
209:by `evals/multi-model-verify/test_kimi_lane_home.py`,
210:`test_kimi_lane_login.py`, `test_kimi_lane_lock.py` and
211:`test_kimi_credential_state.py`. A debate home reaches the one credential
212:through a directory JUNCTION and must never hold a COPY: the access token
213:lives 900 seconds and a refresh rotates BOTH tokens, so a copy that
214:refreshes retires the original. Change the tests first.
215:
216:The same builder asserts, as a POSTCONDITION on its own act, that the
217:`skills/` directory it just created is empty. That is NOT a per-round
218:control and must not be described as one: nothing re-checks it at
219:dispatch, and every writer into that directory sits in the builder
220:itself - the `New-Item` that creates it, and the two seams below it. Its
221:cases are in `test_kimi_lane_home.py`. Those two seams are builder
222:contract rather than test scaffolding. They are gated on environment
223:variables, so any parent process can set them; no shipped caller does,
224:and either one can only force the build to FAIL, never turn a failing
225:build into a successful one.
226:
227:A pin that matches the RAW file text needs its phrase unbroken on ONE
228:PHYSICAL LINE; a pin built on the whitespace-normalized read does not.
229:Both forms are in use, in the same test file, and nothing marks which is
230:which. So REFLOWING A PARAGRAPH CAN TURN A PIN RED WITHOUT CHANGING A
231:WORD, and the failure names the pin rather than the wrap. Measured
232:2026-08-19: one task was blocked twice on this, once when an edit made a
233:pinned clause sentence-initial (the pins are case-sensitive) and once when
234:the rewrap split the phrase across lines. Check which read a pin uses
235:before editing near it, and prefer restructuring the prose to keep an
236:existing pin green over editing the pin to fit new prose.
237:
238:Contract text inside `contract:start` / `contract:end` HTML comment
239:markers must sit WHOLE inside a single pin in `evals/multi-model-verify/`.
240:The checker scans all Markdown under `skills/`, plus `agents/*.md` and
241:`commands/*.md`.
242:
243:A pin is a string literal in one of exactly three assertion clause forms:
244:
245:- `"literal" in body`
246:- `body.count("literal")`, alone or compared `== n` or `>= n` with n at
247:  least 1, or `> n` with n at least 0
248:- an `and`, which contributes every operand it recognizes, so
249:  `"literal" in body and flag` still pins the literal
250:
251:The needle must be a plain string literal. Adjacent literals across
252:several lines are fine, because the parser folds them into one.
253:
254:The assertion must also be able to FAIL the suite. An assertion whose
255:failure is deliberately caught proves the opposite of what it looks
256:like, so it pins nothing: inside a `raises(...)` or `suppress(...)`
257:block, inside the body of a `try` that has handlers, or in a function
258:marked xfail. A `try/finally` has no handlers, so its body still pins.
259:
260:Nothing else counts, and the rule matches a COMPLETE clause rather than
261:looking for these shapes anywhere in the expression. A string locks
262:nothing if it sits in a docstring, in an assertion's failure message,
263:under `not`, in a `not in` comparison, on either side of an `or`, in a
264:count comparison outside the positive bounds above, such as `== 0` or
265:`>= 0`, in a plain equality such as `result == "text"`, in a regex such
266:as `re.search(...)`, in either branch of a conditional, or is reached
267:through a variable name. Any positive assertion outside the three forms
268:above is rejected, whatever it means.
269:In every one of those cases the checker reports the region as unlocked,
270:which is a red; it never reads as covered.
271:
272:`test_contract_coverage.py` enforces this and lists any region that is
273:not locked. A region too long for one pin is two regions. Adding or
274:removing a marked region also means editing `DECLARED_REGIONS` in that
275:file, which is what makes deleting a region visible.

612:    [Array]::Sort($unique, [System.StringComparer]::Ordinal)
613:    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
614:    $out = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
615:    foreach ($rel in $unique) {
616:        # A failed ReadAllBytes is NON-TERMINATING on both hosts
617:        # (measured 2026-08-04), so without this catch $bytes keeps the
618:        # PREVIOUS file's contents and this line records that hash for
619:        # the file it could not read - deterministically, so the wrong
620:        # value reproduces on every later run. Evidence that quietly
621:        # names the wrong bytes is worse than no evidence.
622:        $bytes = $null
623:        try {
624:            $bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Join-Path $repo $rel))
625:        } catch {
626:            $sha.Dispose()
627:            return @{ Error = ("'" + $rel + "' could not be read: " +
628:                               $_.Exception.Message) }
629:        }
630:        $hex = ([System.BitConverter]::ToString($sha.ComputeHash($bytes)) -replace '-', '').ToLower()
631:        [void]$out.Add($rel + " " + $hex)
632:    }
633:    return @{ Paths = @($out) }
634:}
635:
636:function Get-HeadSha($repo) {
637:    # @{Ok=$true; Sha=..} or @{Ok=$false; Reason=..}. Structured for the
638:    # same reason every other capture here is: a bare empty string cannot
639:    # be told apart from a failed read, and an unread HEAD must never
640:    # compare equal to anything.
641:    $out = (& git -C $repo rev-parse HEAD 2>$null | Out-String).Trim()
642:    if (($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) -or -not $out) {
643:        return @{ Ok = $false; Reason = "could not resolve HEAD in $repo" }
644:    }
645:    return @{ Ok = $true; Sha = $out }
646:}
647:
648:function Get-CombinedSha256($fields, $manifestLines) {
649:    # ONE digest over a raw status capture's fields plus a content
650:    # manifest's lines, NUL-joined - the separator git already emits
651:    # them with, so no field value can forge a boundary. Shared by the
652:    # source-side fingerprint below and the mirror-side one at
653:    # construction and verify time, so the two are computed the same way
654:    # by construction rather than by two call sites staying in sync.
655:    $joined = ((@($fields) + @($manifestLines)) -join "`0")
656:    $bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($joined)
657:    $sha = [System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create()
658:    try { $digest = $sha.ComputeHash($bytes) } finally { $sha.Dispose() }
659:    return (($digest | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString("x2") }) -join "")
660:}

662:function Get-StatusSha256($repo) {
663:    # A non-HEAD fingerprint for whichever repo it is given: the SAME
664:    # status capture the mirror already uses, PLUS the content manifest
665:    # of the paths that status names, combined by Get-CombinedSha256.
666:    # Used on the SOURCE for source_status_sha256 and on the MIRROR
667:    # itself for mirror_state_sha256 - one algorithm, so the two
668:    # fingerprints cannot drift apart by drifting the code that computes
669:    # them.
670:    #
671:    # THE CONTENT HALF IS NOT OPTIONAL, and measured 2026-08-04 rather
672:    # than assumed: editing an already-ignored file leaves the status
673:    # listing byte-identical, so a status-only fingerprint verified clean
674:    # across exactly the drift this check exists to catch. Status alone
675:    # sees a path APPEAR or DISAPPEAR or change code; it does not see the
676:    # bytes behind it change, and the bytes are the review input.
677:    $captured = Get-BaselineRaw $repo
678:    if (-not $captured.Ok) {
679:        return @{ Ok = $false; Reason = $captured.Reason }
680:    }
681:    $parsedStatus = ConvertTo-StatusRecord $captured.Fields
682:    if ($parsedStatus.ContainsKey("Error")) {
683:        return @{ Ok = $false; Reason = $parsedStatus.Error }
684:    }
685:    $subj = Get-ManifestSubject $parsedStatus.Records
686:    if ($subj.ContainsKey("Error")) {
687:        return @{ Ok = $false; Reason = $subj.Error }
688:    }
689:    $content = Get-ContentManifest $repo $subj.Paths
690:    if ($content.ContainsKey("Error")) {
691:        return @{ Ok = $false; Reason = $content.Error }
692:    }
693:    return @{ Ok = $true
694:              Sha = (Get-CombinedSha256 $captured.Fields $content.Paths) }
695:}

574:            print("file: cannot read %s: not UTF-8" % path)
575:            return 2
576:        pointer_path = Path(args.pointer) if args.pointer else repo_root / OLD_PATH
577:        try:
578:            pointer = decode_utf8(pointer_path.read_bytes())
579:        except OSError:
580:            pointer = None
581:        label = str(path)
582:    if args.digests:
583:        try:
584:            doc = parse(text)
585:        except ParseError as exc:
586:            print("file: cannot parse %s: %s" % (label, exc))
587:            return 2
588:        for item in doc.items:
589:            print("%s %s" % (item.id, canonical_digest(item, doc)))
590:        return 0
591:    return lint_text(text, pointer, repo_root=repo_root, revision=args.revision,
592:                     today=today, label=label)

595:def is_governed(path):
596:    path = path.replace("\\", "/")
597:    return path in GOVERNED_FILES or any(path.startswith(p) for p in GOVERNED_PREFIXES)

600:def _verified_map(text):
601:    if text is None:
602:        return {}
603:    try:
604:        doc = parse(text)
605:    except ParseError:
606:        return {}
607:    return {item.id: (item.status, item.get("Verified")) for item in doc.items}

610:def reattested_items(old_text, new_text):
611:    """Ids re-attested between the two texts, in two forms.
612:
613:    An item that is OPEN or PARTIAL in the new text counts when its
614:    Verified field changed or the item is new. An item that is DONE or
615:    GONE in the new text counts when it was OPEN or PARTIAL in the old
616:    one, OR when it is new AND the old text was readable, reported either
617:    way as '<id> (closed)':
618:    closing an item IS an attestation about the governed work that closed
619:    it, and being born closed is that same attestation made in one step
620:    instead of two.
621:
622:    The second form is a DELIBERATE WIDENING of the spec's 3b and 3c
623:    wording, which speaks only of a re-attested OPEN or PARTIAL item.
624:    Without it a wave whose only backlog change is a close could never
625:    satisfy the Stop hook or the pre-push clause.
626:
627:    The NEW-and-closed half of it was added 2026-09-05, after a session
628:    did governed work, filed the item that owned it as DONE, and was
629:    still refused: the old condition asked whether the id had been OPEN
630:    BEFORE, which an item that did not exist can never satisfy. Work
631:    filed and closed in one session was unattestable, and the remedies
632:    the refusal left were to mis-state the item as OPEN or to refresh
633:    some other item that does not own the work.
634:
635:    Everything else is unchanged: a Verified edit on an item that is DONE
636:    in BOTH texts does not count, and an unrelated byte does not count.
637:    """
638:    old = _verified_map(old_text)
639:    new = _verified_map(new_text)
640:    # "NEW" only means anything against an old text that EXISTS. With no
641:    # readable old text every item is trivially new, and counting the
642:    # closed ones would make the gate satisfiable by a backlog nobody
643:    # touched. The first version of the born-closed widening missed this
644:    # and turned test_absent_old_text_counts_every_open_item red, which
645:    # is the guard working.
646:    have_old = bool(old)
647:    out = []
648:    for item_id, (status, verified) in new.items():
649:        if status in OPEN_STATUSES:
650:            if item_id not in old or old[item_id][1] != verified:
651:                out.append(item_id)
652:        elif status in ("DONE", "GONE"):
653:            was_open = item_id in old and old[item_id][0] in OPEN_STATUSES
654:            born_closed = have_old and item_id not in old
655:            if was_open or born_closed:
656:                out.append("%s (closed)" % item_id)
657:    return out

660:def range_check(repo_root, range_spec, today):
661:    """The governed-range clause: if the range touched a governed path,
662:    BACKLOG.md must carry a re-attested item. `reattested_items` decides
663:    what counts, and it deliberately widens the spec's 3b/3c wording so a
664:    CLOSE (OPEN or PARTIAL becoming DONE or GONE) counts too."""
665:    if ".." in range_spec:
666:        base, head = range_spec.split("..", 1)
667:        if not base or not head:
668:            print("range %s: malformed" % range_spec)
669:            return 2
670:        # --no-renames: with rename detection on, a governed file moved to an
671:        # ungoverned path is listed only at its destination and the governed
672:        # side of the change disappears from the listing.
673:        changed = git_output(repo_root, "diff", "--no-renames", "--name-only",
674:                             base, head)
675:        old_text = read_at_revision(repo_root, base, BACKLOG_PATH)
676:    else:
677:        head = range_spec
678:        changed = git_output(repo_root, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--root",
679:                             "--no-renames", "-r", "--name-only", head)
680:        parent_out = git_output(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", head + "^")
681:        parent = (accept_exactly_one_nonempty_line(parent_out)
682:                  if parent_out is not None else None)
683:        old_text = (read_at_revision(repo_root, parent, BACKLOG_PATH)
684:                    if parent else None)
685:    if changed is None:
686:        print("range %s: git could not list the changed paths" % range_spec)
687:        return 2
688:    paths = [p for p in changed.splitlines() if p]
689:    governed = [p for p in paths if is_governed(p)]
690:    new_text = read_at_revision(repo_root, head, BACKLOG_PATH)
691:    code = 0
692:    if governed:
693:        ids = reattested_items(old_text, new_text)
694:        if not ids:
695:            print("range %s: governed paths changed (%s) and no OPEN or PARTIAL "
696:                  "item was re-attested (a refreshed Verified line, or the item "
697:                  "closed to DONE or GONE)" % (range_spec, ", ".join(governed)))
698:            code = 1
699:        else:
700:            print("range %s: governed paths changed (%s); re-attested: %s"
701:                  % (range_spec, ", ".join(governed), ", ".join(ids)))
702:    if BACKLOG_PATH in paths:
703:        if new_text is None:
704:            print("range %s: %s deleted at %s" % (range_spec, BACKLOG_PATH, head))
705:            return 1
706:        pointer = read_at_revision(repo_root, head, OLD_PATH)
707:        lint_code = lint_text(new_text, pointer, repo_root=repo_root, revision=head,
708:                              today=today, label="%s@%s" % (BACKLOG_PATH, head))
709:        if lint_code != 0:
710:            code = 1

140:def parse(text):
141:    lines = text.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
142:    preamble, groups, items = [], [], []
143:    section = "preamble"
144:    current_item = None
145:    current_group = None
146:    in_header = False
147:    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
148:        if line == "## Ranking":
149:            if section != "preamble":
150:                raise ParseError("line %d: a second Ranking section" % (index + 1))
151:            section = "ranking"
152:            continue
153:        heading = HEADING_RE.match(line)
154:        if heading:
155:            section = "items"
156:            current_item = Item(id=heading.group(1), title=heading.group(2),
157:                                heading=line, line=index + 1)
158:            items.append(current_item)
159:            in_header = True
160:            continue
161:        if ANY_H2_RE.match(line):
162:            raise ParseError("line %d: heading is neither Ranking nor an item: %r"
163:                             % (index + 1, line))
164:        if section == "preamble":
165:            preamble.append(line)
166:        elif section == "ranking":
167:            group = GROUP_RE.match(line)
168:            # A header whose text is only spaces or tabs is not "`### `
169:            # followed by text" (spec 1b); it falls through as a stray line.
170:            if group and group.group(1).strip(" \t") != "":
171:                current_group = Group(raw_header=line,
172:                                      name=group.group(1).strip(" \t"))
173:                groups.append(current_group)
174:                continue
175:            if line.strip(" \t") == "":
176:                continue
177:            rank = RANK_RE.match(line)
178:            if current_group is None:
179:                stray = Group(raw_header="", name="")
180:                groups.append(stray)
181:                current_group = stray
182:            if rank:
183:                current_group.ids.append(rank.group(1))
184:            else:
185:                current_group.stray_lines.append(line)
186:        else:
187:            if in_header:
188:                match = FIELD_RE.match(line)
189:                if match:
190:                    current_item.fields.append((match.group(1), match.group(2)))
191:                    continue
192:                in_header = False
193:            current_item.body.append(line)
194:    if section == "preamble":
195:        raise ParseError("no '## Ranking' section")
196:    return Document(preamble=preamble, groups=groups, items=items)

199:def canonical_bytes(item, doc):
200:    """The byte-exact canonical content the spec's 1c defines."""
201:    lines = [item.heading]
202:    lines += ["%s: %s" % (k, v) for k, v in item.fields if k != "Verified"]
203:    lines += item.body
204:    lines = [strip_trailing(ln) for ln in lines]
205:    while lines and lines[-1] == "":
206:        lines.pop()
207:    group = doc.group_of(item.id)
208:    group_text = "" if group is None else group.raw_header[3:].strip(" \t")
209:    text = "\n".join(lines) + "\n" + "group:" + group_text + "\n"
210:    return text.encode("utf-8")

213:def canonical_digest(item, doc):
214:    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(item, doc)).hexdigest()[:12]

217:def rule_7_verified(item, doc, today):
218:    value = item.get("Verified")
219:    if value is None:
220:        return []  # rule 1 already reports the missing field
221:    match = VERIFIED_RE.match(value)
222:    if not match:
223:        return ["item %s: rule 7 (verified digest): Verified must be "
224:                "'YYYY-MM-DD <12 hex>', got %r" % (item.id, value)]
225:    try:
226:        stamp = datetime.date.fromisoformat(match.group(1))
227:    except ValueError:
228:        return ["item %s: rule 7 (verified digest): invalid date %s"
229:                % (item.id, match.group(1))]
230:    out = []
231:    if stamp > today:
232:        out.append("item %s: rule 7 (verified digest): date %s is in the future"
233:                   % (item.id, match.group(1)))
234:    expected = canonical_digest(item, doc)
235:    if match.group(2) != expected:
236:        out.append("item %s: rule 7 (verified digest): content changed since "
237:                   "attestation; expected digest %s" % (item.id, expected))
238:    return out

242:    """Return stdout of a git command, or None on a non-zero exit or a
243:    missing git binary."""
244:    try:
245:        proc = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=str(repo_root),
246:                              capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")

280:def in_tree_path(value):
281:    """A Record: path must be repository-relative: not absolute, not
282:    drive-rooted, and with no `..` segment. `..` alone would otherwise
283:    satisfy an existence check from inside any repository."""
284:    normalized = value.replace("\\", "/")
285:    if normalized == "" or normalized.startswith("/") or re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", normalized):
286:        return False
287:    return ".." not in normalized.split("/")

293:    if revision is None:
294:        root = Path(repo_root).resolve()
295:        target = (root / path).resolve()
296:        if target != root and root not in target.parents:
297:            return False
298:        return target.exists()
299:    return git_output(repo_root, "cat-file", "-e", "%s:%s" % (revision, path)) is not None
